verdict.summary: Google Workspace provides instant self-serve setup for development and internal apps, but public distribution or requests for sensitive and restricted scopes require mandatory Google OAuth verification and third-party security assessments (CASA).

evidence.note: Public apps requiring sensitive or restricted scopes must undergo verification and CASA assessments.

verification.note: Jeśli aplikacja wymaga zakresów wrażliwych lub ograniczonych, konieczne jest przejście procesu weryfikacji i oceny bezpieczeństwa (CASA).

evidence.note: Setting up Google Cloud projects, configuring consent screens, and implementing server-side OAuth flow typically takes 1 to 3 hours.

wait_days.applies_to: Applies to public applications requesting sensitive or restricted scopes requiring verification or CASA security assessments.

evidence.note: Google does not publish a fixed SLA for verification or CASA reviews; community reports suggest ranges from several days to multiple weeks.

verification.note: Source mentions the verification and security assessment processes can take several weeks or longer, but does not state the exact 3 to 42 days range.

blockers.description: Third-party security assessment through Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA) framework validated by a Designated Lab.
blockers.applies_when: When requesting restricted scopes or certain sensitive scopes handling user data.

evidence.note: Apps requesting restricted scopes must undergo a CASA security assessment. [auto-check: only non-official sources (e.g. third-party blogs), so treated as inferred]

verification.note: No source cited for this claim, so there is nothing to check.

blockers.description: A demo video showing the user journey, consent screen, and feature usage matching requested scopes.
blockers.applies_when: When submitting an app for Google OAuth verification.

evidence.note: Google requires a demo video explaining why scopes and data are needed during verification.

verification.note: For the verification, you must submit a demo video showing the user journey or flow explaining the use of requested permissions or data.

prerequisites.item: Google Cloud Platform account and project

evidence.note: Developers must register their OAuth app in the Google Cloud Console.

verification.note: Any application that calls Google APIs needs to enable those APIs in the API Console. If prompted, select a project, or create a new one.

steps.title: Create or Select a Google Cloud Project
steps.detail: Go to the Google Cloud Console and create or select your project.
steps.notes: Requires a human logged into the Google Cloud Console.

evidence.note: Projects are managed directly in the Google Cloud Console.

verification.note: If prompted, select a project, or create a new one.

steps.title: Enable Required Workspace APIs
steps.detail: Enable specific Google Workspace APIs your AI agent needs (e.g., Gmail, Calendar, Drive) in the API Library.
steps.notes: Can be done via Cloud Console interface.

evidence.note: APIs must be enabled in the API library.

verification.note: Any application that calls Google APIs needs to enable those APIs in the API Console.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen
steps.detail: Set up branding, app name, user support email, developer contact email, and choose user type (Internal vs External).
steps.notes: Requires entering metadata and agreeing to User Data Policy.

evidence.note: Consent screen configuration is done via Google Auth platform settings.

verification.note: En Información de la aplicación, en Nombre de la aplicación, ingresa un Nombre... En Correo electrónico de asistencia... En Público, selecciona el tipo de usuario... En Información de contacto...

steps.title: Declare Authorization Scopes
steps.detail: Select and declare the authorization scopes required for your integration under Data Access / Scopes.
steps.notes: Ensure exact scope strings match the code implementation.

evidence.note: Scopes are configured on the consent screen.

verification.note: Para definir el nivel de acceso otorgado a tu app, debes identificar y declarar los alcances de autorización.

steps.title: Create OAuth Client ID Credentials
steps.detail: Navigate to Credentials > Create Credentials > OAuth client ID, select Web application, and register authorized redirect URIs.
steps.notes: Download the client_secret.json for backend storage.

evidence.note: Web application credentials are created in the Credentials menu.

verification.note: Go to the Clients page. Click Create Client. Select the Web application application type. Fill in the form and click Create... specify authorized redirect URIs.

steps.title: Implement OAuth Flow in Backend
steps.detail: Write server-side code to handle authorization redirection, token exchange using client credentials, offline access, and refresh token storage.
steps.notes: Agent can fully write and test OAuth handling logic.

evidence.note: Standard web server flow guidelines apply.

verification.note: This document explains how web server applications use Google API Client Libraries or Google OAuth 2.0 endpoints to implement OAuth 2.0 authorization...

steps.title: Submit for Verification and Security Assessment (If Applicable)
steps.detail: If using sensitive or restricted scopes publicly, prepare a demo video, privacy policy, and submit through the Google verification console (and complete CASA if required).
steps.notes: Requires human submission, compliance documentation, and third-party security lab engagement.

evidence.note: Restricted scopes trigger mandatory verification and CASA assessment.

verification.note: If your application accesses Google user data with the Google APIs and requests certain scopes, you might have to complete the Google verification process and a separate security assessment process.

probes.summary: OpenID Connect discovery document found (issuer: https://accounts.google.com).
RFC 8414 authorization server metadata found (issuer: https://accounts.google.com).
Authorization endpoint (from docs) responds to a request with a fake client_id (HTTP 200, redirected to https://accounts.google.com/signin/oauth/error); response mentions an OAuth/client error.
Token endpoint (from docs) is live: an unauthenticated request with a fake code returned OAuth error "invalid_client" (HTTP 401).
Discovery metadata does not advertise a registration_endpoint, so dynamic client registration is likely unsupported.
Page loads (HTTP 200), redirected to https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification?hl=pt-br — appears to require sign-in.
Page loads (HTTP 200), redirected to https://developers.google.com/workspace/marketplace/configure-oauth-consent-screen?hl=zh-tw — appears to require sign-in.
Link loads (HTTP 200) — redirects to sign-in, as expected for a developer console.

limitations: No accounts were created, no forms submitted, no OAuth apps registered, and no credentials were used. Probes are unauthenticated GET requests against public discovery documents, endpoints and documentation pages, plus one unauthenticated POST to the token endpoint with a fake authorization code and a nonexistent client_id (to confirm it answers with an OAuth error).
